record.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis

record.description: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at the reference point whose major radius is the reference major radius, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
record.documentation:
Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at a specified reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The reference point has major radius equal to the [reference major radius](name:reference_major_radius).

The defining projection is:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}})
$$

where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the toroidal reference magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}=(R_{\mathrm{ref}},\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},Z_{\mathrm{ref}})$ is the full reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$. For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the value is independent of $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$.

This quantity is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field). It is distinct from [toroidal magnetic field at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis), from the magnetic-field magnitude, and from [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field).

Sign convention: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
record.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field

record.description: Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of toroidal magnetic field through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the plasma boundary, including externally imposed and plasma-poloidal-current contributions.
record.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of the toroidal magnetic-field component through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the plasma boundary. It is the boundary value of toroidal magnetic flux used to define toroidal-flux radial labels.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, the boundary toroidal flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b} = \int_{\Omega_b} \mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} B_\phi(R,Z)\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} \frac{F(\psi(R,Z))}{R}\, dA_{RZ}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ is this boundary toroidal flux, $\Omega_b$ is the boundary-enclosed region in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B_\phi$ is its toroidal component in tesla, $dA_{RZ}$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area element in square meters, $F(\psi)=R B_\phi$ is the poloidal-current function in tesla meters, and $\psi$ is the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux label.

The geometric measure of $\Omega_b$ is the [poloidal cross-sectional area of the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_boundary). $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ includes both externally imposed toroidal-field flux and the contribution associated with plasma poloidal current, and is distinct from [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary due to poloidal current](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current), which contains only that plasma-current contribution. It also differs from [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which is magnetic flux through a horizontal disk rather than through the boundary-enclosed poloidal cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal magnetic field threading the plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
record.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary

record.description: Ratio of the squared gradient magnitude of the length-valued toroidal-flux coordinate to squared major radius, defining a local equilibrium metric coefficient.
record.documentation:
Ratio of the squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to squared major radius is a local equilibrium metric coefficient. It encodes flux-surface spacing with inverse-square major-radius weighting.

The defining relation is:

$$
G = \frac{|\nabla \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}|^2}{R^2}
$$

where $G$ is this local coefficient, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the length-valued toroidal-flux coordinate, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical height.

The toroidal-flux coordinate retains its prescribed scale; no boundary normalization or substitution of an arbitrary flux label is implied. The denominator is squared major radius, not its inverse. The squared gradient magnitude distinguishes this coefficient from inverse squared major radius alone.

This quantity is a pointwise ratio without spatial averaging. Its flux-surface-averaged counterpart averages the complete ratio over a closed magnetic flux surface; it is not the ratio of separately averaged numerator and denominator.

$$a/b$$

The magnitude is the Euclidean norm of a vector quantity, or the modulus of a complex one.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The square is a scalar quantity multiplied by itself, or a vector's dot product with itself.
record.name: ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius

record.description: Toroidal total current density is the net conventional charge flux per unit area around the symmetry axis, formed by algebraically summing all included current contributions.
record.documentation:
Toroidal total current density is the signed local projection of the net [current density](name:current_density) onto the toroidal direction. It combines all included contributions before or after projection onto that same direction.

The projection and aggregation are defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_k \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_k
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal total current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total current-density vector, $\mathbf{j}_k$ is an included current-density contribution, and $k$ labels those contributions. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional charge transport is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, counterclockwise when viewed from above along the negative vertical direction.

record.documentation:
Tungsten-ion number density is the particle count per unit volume for all positively charged tungsten ions, with neutral tungsten excluded. It may denote a local value or a spatially averaged value over a defined domain.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge state. Specific instances include [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), [tungsten density at magnetic axis](name:tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [tungsten density at divertor target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target); these differ by evaluation locus or averaging domain. Neutral tungsten is not included.

record.description: Dimensionless shape parameter for the plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section, expressing the aggregate inward radial displacement of its upper and lower extrema relative to the geometric center.
record.documentation:
Plasma-boundary triangularity is a dimensionless shaping parameter describing the asymmetry of the boundary’s poloidal cross-section through the inward displacement of its upper and lower radial extrema relative to the geometric center. It characterizes the complete boundary rather than either half-plane extremum alone.

For the upper and lower boundary extrema, the aggregate triangularity is defined as

$$
\delta = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{R_0-R_u}{a}+\frac{R_0-R_l}{a}\right)
$$

where $\delta$ is the plasma-boundary triangularity, $R_0$ is the major-radius coordinate of the geometric center, $R_u$ and $R_l$ are the plasma-boundary triangularity, $R_0$ is the major-radius coordinate of the geometric center, $R_u$ and $R_l$ are the major-radius coordinates of the upper and lower boundary extrema, and $a$ is the boundary minor radius. The coordinates refer to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the entire plasma boundary and aggregates the upper and lower extremal displacements into one shape parameter. It excludes the separately resolved [upper triangularity of the plasma boundary](name:upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower triangularity of the plasma boundary](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), which retain only one extremum. It also differs from [triangularity of a flux surface](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface), which describes an individual nested magnetic flux surface rather than the outer plasma boundary.
record.name: triangularity_of_plasma_boundary

record.description: Vertical coordinate of a plasma filament geometry point, giving its signed height from the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
record.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of a plasma filament geometry point specifies its signed height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the specified point relative to the coordinate origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the positive symmetry-axis direction.

The specified point is the reference point for an oblique cross-section or the second endpoint of the central segment for a thick-line cross-section. The quantity applies to one filament geometry point, not an average over filaments or a coordinate of the plasma boundary. Unlike the [vertical outline of a plasma filament](name:vertical_outline_of_plasma_filament), it specifies a point location rather than a contour.

Sign convention: Positive when the specified point lies on the positive-$Z$ side of the zero-height plane.
record.name: vertical_coordinate_of_plasma_filament

record.description: Signed vertical height of each point on the plasma-boundary outline in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, defining its poloidal cross-sectional shape.
record.documentation:
The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height of each point on the plasma-boundary contour in a poloidal cross-section. It describes the boundary geometry rather than a field, flux, or scalar boundary summary.

The coordinate is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Each outline point has its own $Z$ value; the quantity is neither an average nor an extremum over the boundary.

This quantity
record.name: vertical_outline_of_plasma_boundary

record.description: The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an elliptic shatter cone is its projection in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
record.documentation:
The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an elliptic shatter cone is the projection of that major-axis direction onto the $y$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The major-axis direction is the orientation of the principal semiaxis of the cone's elliptic cross-section.

The component is defined by

$$
e_{\mathrm{maj},y} = \hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ is the y component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ is the unit vector along the major axis of the elliptic shatter cone, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity applies to the geometry of an elliptic shatter cone and to the major semiaxis orientation of its elliptic cross-section; its aggregation convention is none, because it is a single vector component rather than a sum or mean. It is distinct from the unsigned major-axis length, from the [y component of the shatter-cone direction unit vector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes the cone direction rather than the major-axis orientation, and from the [y component of the minor-axis unit vector](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which refers to the orthogonal minor semiaxis.

Together with the [x component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z component](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this quantity forms the Cartesian representation of $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$; the linked x and z components and $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ satisfy $(e_{\mathrm{maj},x})^2 + (e_{\mathrm{maj},y})^2 + (e_{\mathrm{maj},z})^2 = 1$, where $e_{\mathrm{maj},x}$ and $e_{\mathrm{maj},z}$ are the linked x and z components. The major-axis and minor-axis unit vectors jointly orient the elliptic cone and satisfy $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot \hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}} = 0$, where $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}}$ is the minor-axis unit vector with [x](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), [y](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), and [z](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) components.

Sign convention: Positive when $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ has a component in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.
record.name: y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone

record.description: Lower photon-energy boundary of an X-ray detection or emission energy band, expressed in eV. For photon counting, it is the threshold assigned to the specified detector pixel or channel: an incident photon is eligible for counting only if its energy exceeds this value. For an emissivity profile, it specifies the lower boundary of the emission band, assumed common to all channels used in the profile reconstruction.
record.documentation: This quantity specifies the low-energy edge of a spectral window, paired with upper_photon_energy at the high-energy edge. A detector threshold applies individually to its pixel or channel, not as a detector-wide average. It is a band boundary rather than a representative pixel energy or a photon-energy calibration coordinate, and is not restricted to the spectral bandpass of a crystal-spectrometer pixel. The strict counting condition is E_gamma > E_gamma,min; exceeding the threshold is necessary for counting but does not imply unit detection efficiency. For emission profiles, the quantity instead delimits the included emission band without imposing a detector-counting interpretation.
record.name: lower_bound_photon_energy

record.description: Dimensionless ratio T_p/T_ref, obtained by dividing the kinetic temperature T_p of a selected particle species by the positive reference temperature T_ref for the same magnetic flux surface in a local gyrokinetic flux-tube simulation. The unit is 1.
record.documentation: This scalar expresses a selected species' kinetic temperature relative to the simulation's reference thermal scale; the species may be an ion species or electrons. Unlike an absolute particle temperature, its value depends on the specified reference temperature. Unlike magnetic-axis electron- or ion-temperature peaking ratios, it does not compare a magnetic-axis temperature with a volume-averaged temperature.
record.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature

record.documentation: No source is bound to this quantity, so the scale of the toroidal-flux coordinate and the gradient convention cannot be established. These are needed to define the squared gradient magnitude consistently with the declared unit 1: a physical-space gradient of a length-valued coordinate is dimensionless, whereas that of a dimensionless flux coordinate has inverse-length dimension. The neighbouring records do not establish the convention used for this target.
record.name: square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude

record.description: Dimensionless collisionality for a specified pair of particle species, obtained by dividing their collision frequency by the characteristic transit frequency: nu_ab_star = nu_ab / nu_transit. Both frequencies have reciprocal-time units, and the resulting quantity has unit 1.
record.documentation: This quantity describes the strength of collisional relaxation between two specified particle species relative to transit motion in the local gyrokinetic model. Its species-pair indices identify the interacting populations. Unlike the collision frequency itself, it is dimensionless. It is not restricted to electrons or to the pedestal top, and its characteristic-transit-frequency normalization differs from the trapped-electron bounce-frequency normalization used by the neighbouring electron-collisionality records.
record.name: collisionality_between_species

record.description: A Fourier coefficient of the component of the non-axisymmetric vacuum error magnetic field normal to a specified control surface, obtained by Fourier decomposition of that normal component over the surface points. The coefficient has unit T. The source does not specify the Fourier normalization, phase convention, or angular coordinates.
record.documentation: This quantity represents a coefficient in the Fourier decomposition, rather than a local normal-field value or the full magnetic-field vector. The projection is normal to the specified control surface, not the cylindrical radial or toroidal component; the source does not require the control surface to be a magnetic flux surface. It describes the non-axisymmetric vacuum error field rather than the total field including plasma contributions.
record.name: normal_non_axisymmetric_vacuum_magnetic_field_fourier_coefficient_at_control_surface

record.description: Signed effective number of turns assigned to one cross-section element of a passive conducting loop for calculating the loop's magnetic field. It weights the element's current contribution, with positive turns meaning that positive current circulates counter-clockwise when seen from above. The quantity is dimensionless, with unit 1.
record.documentation: This quantity applies to an individual passive-loop cross-section element, not to an aggregate over the elements comprising a loop. Its magnitude represents the element's effective winding contribution to magnetic-field calculations, and its sign specifies orientation under the counter-clockwise-from-above convention. It is distinct from the passive-loop current that it weights and from the element's conducting cross-sectional area. Unlike the effective turn count of a coil conductor element, it describes an element of a passive axisymmetric conductor loop that is not actively driven by a power supply.
record.name: turn_count_of_passive_loop_element

record.documentation: The supplied definition identifies the same quantity as the existing motional_stark_polarization_angle_at_constraint_position: the linear-polarization orientation of motional Stark emission at a constraint position for the specified beam and viewing geometry. No bound source or other supplied distinction supports a separate record.
record.name: motional_stark_polarization_angle_at_constraint_position

record.description: Absolute thermodynamic temperature of a selected sensor, represented by the local temperature at its thermocouple junction and obtained by thermocouple measurement, in K. It applies to one sensor member, not to an average or other aggregation over the sensor set.
record.documentation: This scalar quantity describes the local thermal state at the thermocouple junction of an individual sensor associated with a structural component. The enclosing set of sensors provides collection context only; the value is not a sum or average over that set. Its sensor locus distinguishes it from coolant temperatures at inlet, outlet, or plant-component ports and from temperatures assigned to specifically named hardware such as a neutron detector or coil conductor. It describes thermal state rather than the acceleration, displacement, or strain measured by other structural instrumentation.
record.name: temperature_of_sensor

record.description: Whole-plasma toroidal beta rescaled by plasma size, reference toroidal magnetic field and plasma current: beta_N = 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0[T] / Ip[MA], where beta_N is normalized toroidal beta, beta_tor is the dimensionless ratio of volume-averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure to the reference toroidal magnetic pressure, a is plasma minor radius in metres, B0 is the reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field in tesla, and Ip is net toroidal plasma current in megaamperes. The numerical-unit convention and factor of 100 are part of the definition; the result has unit 1. The signed ratio B0/Ip is retained. Pressure may be determined by equilibrium reconstruction. Unlike normalized toroidal thermal beta, the pressure input is not restricted to thermal pressure.
record.documentation: This global plasma parameter expresses toroidal pressure loading after the conventional current-and-geometry rescaling used in MHD stability and confinement assessment. It differs from toroidal beta by the explicit factor of 100 and the minor-radius, reference-field and inverse-current factors, so retaining “normalized” distinguishes a separate quantity rather than an optional reporting convention. Total pressure includes the represented thermal and nonthermal contributions; using pressure from equilibrium reconstruction changes the pressure estimate, not the normalization. Restricting the input to thermal pressure instead gives normalized toroidal thermal beta. The normalization assumes positive minor radius and nonzero reference field and plasma current, without replacing the signed field or current by its magnitude.
record.name: normalized_toroidal_beta

record.description: The externally generated inductive electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage, in V. It is obtained from Faraday's law as V_ext(t) = -dPhi_ext(t)/dt, where Phi_ext is the poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and generated by active coils and magnetically coupled passive conducting structures. Positive voltage denotes an electromotive force with a positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the external-source contribution rather than the total loop voltage at the plasma boundary; it excludes resistive voltage drops and other non-inductive contributions. External sources include both active coil circuits and induced currents in passive conducting structures. Unlike average_external_loop_voltage, which is defined from a prescribed average flux applied by external poloidal-field coils, this quantity is defined from the external flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit, without a prescribed averaging operation.
record.name: external_loop_voltage

record.documentation: No source is bound to this target. The incumbent name denotes neutron number flux, while its definition and unit describe neutron kinetic-energy flux. Without source text establishing which quantity is intended, the name–definition conflict cannot be resolved reliably.

record.description: Major-radius coordinate R of a specified reference point in a poloidal-field coil's cross-sectional geometry, measured in m as the nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis. It is given by R = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), where x and y are the transverse coordinates of that point in a right-handed Cartesian frame whose z axis coincides with the toroidal symmetry axis. The reference point is the annulus centre or the first or second endpoint of the central segment defining a thick-line geometry, as specified by the source.
record.documentation: This scalar locates a reference point in the cross-sectional geometry of an active poloidal-field coil, including central-solenoid and shaping coils. For an annular geometry it locates the annulus centre; for a thick-line geometry it locates one endpoint of the central segment used with a perpendicular thickness to define the rectangular approximation. It is not necessarily the coil centre, an average over the coil, or the inner or outer radius measured from an annulus centre. Unlike the radial outline of a poloidal-field coil, it does not describe the complete cross-sectional boundary; its locus is the poloidal-field coil rather than a separately identified conductor cross-section or coil-conductor element.
record.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_field_coil

record.description: Characteristic time, in s, for the decrease of a selected electric-current magnitude during a disruption. Under a linear-threshold convention, the extrapolated full-decay time is [t(f_low) - t(f_high)]/(f_high - f_low), where f_high and f_low are specified fractions of a specified reference current magnitude and t(f) is the time at which the decaying magnitude reaches fraction f. Under an exponential convention, it is the e-folding time tau in I(t) = I_0 exp[-(t - t_0)/tau], where I_0 is the selected current magnitude at reference time t_0.
record.documentation: This scalar describes disruption-driven electric-current decay without restricting the current to the total plasma current or to a particular particle population. The selected current, reference magnitude and decay convention must be specified when reporting a value; a linear extrapolated decay time is not generally equal to an exponential e-folding time. The plasma-current specialization uses the linear 20–80% construction, [t(0.2) - t(0.8)]/0.6, whereas the runaway-electron specialization describes total toroidal runaway-electron current and permits custom linear, fixed 20–80% linear or exponential conventions. Unlike the neighbouring electron-temperature decay times, this quantity describes electric current, not temperature, and does not denote a local current-density decay time.
record.name: decay_time_due_to_disruption

record.description: Lower operational bound on the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve: the smallest gas throughput the valve can reliably deliver. Throughput is Q_g = p_g dV_g/dt, where p_g is the gas pressure at the flow boundary and dV_g/dt is the volumetric flow rate across that boundary. The quantity is expressed in Pa.m^3.s^-1.
record.documentation: This scalar specifies the minimum operating throughput of a valve connecting a gas bottle to pipes. It describes the aggregate gas stream, rather than an individual molecular species, mass flow, or particle-number rate. Unlike gas_flow or gas_flow_of_valve, it specifies a lower operational limit rather than an unrestricted delivered throughput; maximum_gas_flow specifies the corresponding upper limit. The source provides the valve's minimum flow rate but does not specify a measurement or calibration procedure.
record.name: lower_bound_gas_flow

record.description: Local number density of hydrogen ions (H+) in the scrape-off-layer plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, expressed in m^-3. It counts hydrogen ions per unit physical volume, excluding neutral hydrogen, deuterium, tritium and other species. The precise plasma evaluation point relative to the presheath or sheath entrance is not specified by the source.
record.documentation: This is the hydrogen-specific component of density_at_limiter, provided in the source's species-resolved ion-density summary. It distinguishes hydrogen ions from electrons and other ion species at the same limiter location. The limiter locus distinguishes it from hydrogen density evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface or at a divertor target; it does not denote the separatrix–limiter contact point or a distribution along the limiter surface. The source specifies neither a measurement or calculation method nor a more precise evaluation point.
record.name: hydrogen_density_at_limiter

record.description: Incident angle of the local magnetic field with respect to the plasma-facing-component surface at the Langmuir-probe location, expressed in rad. The reference is the surface itself, not its normal; the source specifies no calculation method or signed-angle convention.
record.documentation: This scalar describes magnetic-field incidence on the plasma-facing-component surface at an embedded or reciprocating Langmuir probe. It provides geometric context for interpreting ion saturation current measurements. It is not the mechanical tilt of the probe's own collector surface, the effective collection area of the probe, or the magnetic-field magnitude.
record.name: surface_incident_angle_of_magnetic_field_at_langmuir_probe

record.description: Radial shift of ablated pellet material from its ablation location to its final deposition location attributable to E×B drift. It is obtained as the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at deposition minus that at ablation: Δρ_tor,N = ρ_tor,N,dep − ρ_tor,N,abl. The displacement is dimensionless, with unit 1.
record.documentation: Each value describes the deposition-relative-to-ablation shift of material released at the corresponding point along the pellet path, rather than a displacement integrated along that path. Only the contribution attributed to E×B drift is included. Radial position is represented by the normalized toroidal flux coordinate; the quantity is therefore neither toroidal motion nor a geometric distance, an absolute deposition coordinate, or a drift velocity. It describes redistribution of ablated material, not the injection motion of the pellet.
record.name: radial_displacement_of_pellet_due_to_e_cross_b_drift

record.description: Dimensionless orientation indicator for the equilibrium toroidal magnetic-field component at a flux surface in local gyrokinetic geometry. For nonzero B_phi, it is obtained as s_phi = sgn(B_phi) = B_phi/|B_phi|, where B_phi = B · e_phi and e_phi points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It is +1 along increasing phi and -1 in the opposite direction, and is undefined when B_phi is zero. Unit: 1.
record.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal magnetic-field member of the orientation-indicator concept parity, evaluated for the local gyrokinetic flux-surface description. It retains only the direction of the toroidal field component, not its magnitude, distinguishing it from toroidal_magnetic_field, which has unit T. It does not indicate plasma-current direction or the even or odd reflection symmetry of a gyrokinetic eigenmode or its perturbations.
record.name: parity_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_at_flux_surface

record.documentation: The source identifies the thickness of a single breeder blanket module layer evaluated at the midplane, distinct from total module thickness and upper or lower module-cap thickness. The supplied naming vocabulary has no midplane locus token, so it cannot express the source-required location in the name.

The described quantity is the local curvature radius of a circular arc in a poloidal-field-coil cross-sectional contour, not the coil radius or an annular inner or outer radius. The supplied naming grammar provides no contour-segment locus or curvature-radius construction that expresses this distinction. Retaining radius_of_poloidal_field_coil would preserve the adjudicated mismatch; using radius_of_coil_conductor_element would instead identify an existing neighbour with a different locus.

The source specifies a pixel-resolved processed image of apparent temperature in K, not necessarily the thermodynamic temperature of the surface material and not a regional maximum. The identifying qualifier 'apparent' is absent from the supplied closed vocabulary. Retaining surface_temperature would preserve the adjudicated ambiguity, and the source does not establish an equivalent permitted qualifier.

The supplied definition describes the same post-breakdown, all-species equivalent-electron inventory as the existing accumulated_total_gas_equivalent_electron_count. The equivalent-electron weighting changes what is counted and distinguishes it from a gas-particle count, but adding that distinction would duplicate the existing quantity. No bound source establishes a separate quantity.

record.description: Electrical resistivity of the material of one mobile plasma-facing component unit, expressed in m.ohm. For an isotropic material, it is the scalar coefficient ρ in the local constitutive relation E = ρJ between electric field and conventional conduction-current density.
record.documentation: The source assigns this material property to an individual mobile plasma-facing component unit, rather than to wall material generally, a limiter tile, or a lumped passive-loop resistance. The required mobile-unit scope cannot be expressed using the supplied naming vocabulary: plasma_facing_component is available, but no token or construction is supplied for its mobile-unit specialization. Reusing the incumbent name would retain the scope mismatch identified by the adjudicator.

record.description: Measured angular phase of a probing wave beam, expressed in rad. For the reflectometer and refractometer sources, it is the phase relative to the phase at launch, obtained as the measured phase minus the launch phase using the same phase convention. The refractometer specifically measures the probing-signal envelope phase rather than the carrier phase. For the interferometer source, it is the phase measured at the specified wavelength after correction for fringe jumps. The sources do not specify a common sign convention or wrapped-phase interval.
record.documentation: This quantity describes the phase of the diagnostic probing beam, not the radio-frequency excitation phase of an antenna or antenna strap, the beam's reference frequency, or its wavefront curvature. Reflectometer values are associated with each probing frequency and time slice corresponding to the beginning of a sweep; refractometer values describe the envelope within a frequency bandwidth. Launch referencing and interferometric fringe-jump correction are source-specific specifications of the reported phase, not additional physical loci. Phase is equivalent modulo 2π, while a continuous or fringe-jump-corrected representation may retain accumulated revolutions; the supplied sources do not prescribe a universal phase origin or phasor-sign convention.
record.name: wave_phase_of_wave_beam

record.documentation: The described quantity is already represented by accumulated_total_prefill_gas_equivalent_electron_count: the cumulative prefill gas inventory, summed over all injected species on an equivalent-electron basis. No distinguishing quantity is established by this case file. Retaining gas_count alone would misidentify the counting basis, while adding equivalent_electron would collide with the existing record.

record.description: Cross-sectional area of a plasma current filament element, expressed in m^2. The cross-section's orientation and the method of obtaining its area are not specified.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the area of a filament element's cross-section, rather than its height, width or inclined-side length. Unlike poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_filament, it does not specify that the cross-section lies in the poloidal plane. No particular cross-sectional shape or calculation from the filament dimensions is prescribed.
record.name: area_of_plasma_filament

record.documentation: The source's first inclination angle (alpha) for an individual active poloidal-field-coil element is already represented by the live names alpha_angle_of_poloidal_field_coil and radial_angle_of_poloidal_field_coil, as confirmed by the adjudicator. The element-level source structure does not establish a distinct quantity, so another standard-name record would duplicate those entries. This alpha parameter is distinct from the second inclination represented by tilt_angle_of_coil_conductor_element.

record.description: Net conventional electric current incident on one complete divertor, obtained by integrating charged-particle current density over the union of its target surfaces, with electron and ion contributions combined using their signed charges. The surface normal points from the plasma into the material, so current in that direction is positive. The quantity is measured in A and covers the complete divertor rather than one target or tile.
record.documentation: The divertor current is the scalar surface integral I = ∫S J_ch · n dA, where S comprises all target surfaces of the specified divertor, J_ch = Σs q_s Γ_s is the conventional charged-particle current density, and n points toward the material. It excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current. Unlike current_at_divertor_target and current_of_divertor_tile, it combines contributions across the complete divertor assembly; it is not a sum over every divertor in the device.
record.name: current_of_divertor

record.description: Geometric radial derivative dV/dψ of the cumulative volume V enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its signed, dimensionful poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate ψ, with other coordinates held fixed. It is obtained by differentiating the enclosed-volume profile V(ψ), and is positive when volume increases with increasing ψ. The unit is Wb^-1.m^3.
record.documentation: This equilibrium quantity is specified on the one-dimensional poloidal-flux grid for each time slice. The volume is cumulative from the magnetic axis to the selected flux surface, so dV/dψ describes the change in enclosed volume per change in poloidal magnetic flux, not a shell volume or a local volume density. It differs from the enclosed-volume derivative with respect to the toroidal-flux coordinate by the differentiation coordinate, and from the poloidal cross-sectional-area derivative by the geometric quantity differentiated. Integrating dV/dψ between two poloidal-flux values gives the difference in their enclosed volumes.
record.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate

record.documentation: The case file identifies tritium_prefill_count as an existing live name for this same quantity. Neither accumulation nor the equivalent-electron convention distinguishes a new quantity: both belong in its definition. A separate record would therefore duplicate the live record.
record.name: tritium_prefill_count

record.description: Dimensionless amplitude c_k of a basis term in an angular expansion f(theta) = sum_k c_k b_k(theta) representing the cross-sectional shape of a magnetic flux surface. The coefficient is specified relative to the chosen shape function, angular parameterization, basis and its normalization; no particular harmonic or trigonometric parity is prescribed. The flux surface comprises points sharing a magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration, with psi(R, Z) = const where psi is poloidal magnetic flux. Unit: 1.
record.documentation: This quantity describes an individual angular expansion term for a specified flux surface, rather than a surface average, an enclosed-volume integral or an overall geometric descriptor such as elongation or squareness. A collection of these scalar coefficients is indexed by expansion term, not by spatial direction. The sine coefficient of a flux surface is the specialization to sine terms; this general coefficient does not impose that restriction. Values depend on the chosen representation, so coefficients from different bases or normalization conventions are not necessarily directly comparable.
record.name: coefficient_of_flux_surface

record.description: Radial derivative dV/dρ_tor of the cumulative volume V enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate ρ_tor, with time and other independent coordinates held fixed. The coordinate has unit m, so the derivative has unit m^2.
record.documentation: The enclosed volume is accumulated from the magnetic axis to the selected flux surface, rather than being the volume of a finite shell. This quantity gives the volume increment per increment of the dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate: dV = (dV/dρ_tor)dρ_tor. It is positive on regular nested surfaces when ρ_tor increases outward. It is distinct from the enclosed volume itself, its derivative with respect to poloidal magnetic flux, the corresponding derivative of enclosed poloidal cross-sectional area, and the temporal derivative of this volume derivative. It is a geometric quantity with no species weighting.
record.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate

record.description: Flux-surface-averaged collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume to the co-passing part of a fast-particle distribution from one specified charge state of an ion species, in W.m^-3. The profile is evaluated using the co-passing part of the distribution. Positive values denote energy gain by that fast-particle population; negative values denote energy loss.
record.documentation: This quantity resolves the collisional power received by co-passing fast particles according to the interacting ion species and charge state. The co-passing restriction applies to the fast-particle distribution receiving the power, not to the interacting ion charge state, and the fast particles are not necessarily ions. Unlike the total co-passing fast-particle collisional power density, this quantity includes only the contribution associated with the specified ion charge state, without a sum over ion species or charge states. It differs from the corresponding thermal power density by describing power to the fast-particle population rather than to thermal ions. It is a flux-surface-averaged power per unit volume, not stored energy density or volume-integrated power; the sources do not specify a numerical evaluation method or an averaging weight.
record.name: co_passing_fast_power_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_ion_state

record.description: Elongation of an individual magnetic flux surface is the ratio of the vertical extent to the radial extent of its poloidal cross-section. In the right-handed cylindrical frame (R, phi, Z), with R the major radius and Z the vertical height, it is obtained as kappa = (Z_max - Z_min)/(R_max - R_min), using the coordinate extrema on that cross-section. It is dimensionless, with unit 1, and is neither an average over surfaces nor a radial derivative of elongation; it is not restricted to the plasma boundary.
record.documentation: A flux surface consists of points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration, represented by psi(R, Z) = constant when psi denotes poloidal magnetic flux. Its elongation describes cross-sectional stretching independently of overall size. For an elliptical cross-section it equals the vertical-to-horizontal semi-axis ratio, but the extent-based definition does not require an ellipse. Evaluating this ratio at the plasma boundary gives elongation_of_plasma_boundary, whereas derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_normalized_minor_radius describes its variation between neighboring surfaces. Unlike squareness or poloidal contour length, elongation measures the vertical-to-radial shape ratio.
record.name: elongation_of_flux_surface

record.description: Number of lines (grooves) per unit length of a spectrometer diffraction grating, expressed in m^-1.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the line or groove density of a diffraction grating used in charge-exchange or ultraviolet spectroscopy. Both source descriptions identify the same quantity, using “lines” and “grooves” synonymously. It characterizes the grating rather than its surface curvature, a detector pixel's assigned wavelength, or a spectrometer channel's spectral width or instrument function.
record.name: grating_line_density

record.description: Global rate at which wall pumping removes particles from the plasma, counted in equivalent electrons rather than necessarily as physical electrons. The rate is aggregated over the wall and is dN_e,removed/dt, where N_e,removed is the cumulative number of electron equivalents removed by pumping. Its unit is s^-1.
record.documentation: This scalar quantity describes electron-equivalent exhaust throughput due to wall pumping. Equivalent-electron counting is the reporting convention and does not imply that the pumped particles are physical electrons. Unlike a local electron particle flux, this quantity is a wall-aggregated removal rate, not a rate per unit area or an electrical current. Unlike neutral particle flux at the wall due to pumping, it is not the particle-number throughput of one specified neutral species. It describes removal by pumping rather than particle return through recycling or surface emission.
record.name: electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping

record.description: Mean magnitude of the total equilibrium magnetic field on a closed magnetic flux surface, expressed in T. The local magnitude B = sqrt(B_vector · B_vector) is taken before averaging, and the mean is obtained as ⟨B⟩ = [∮ B dS/|∇ψ|]/[∮ dS/|∇ψ|], where ψ is the poloidal magnetic flux and dS is the surface-area element. Thus the average is normalized by the total inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weight. It is positive for a nonvanishing field, irrespective of the sign convention for the magnetic-field direction.
record.documentation: This scalar describes equilibrium magnetic-field strength as a function of the poloidal flux coordinate. All components contribute to the local magnitude before the flux-surface average is taken; it is not a selected poloidal or parallel component, a perturbation amplitude, a pointwise value, the minimum over the surface, or the magnitude of an averaged field vector. It averages the magnitude itself, rather than its square or inverse square, and therefore differs from the corresponding flux-surface-averaged second and inverse-square moments.
record.name: flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude

record.description: Mean perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis over a complete closed magnetic flux surface, obtained as <R>_psi = (∮ R dS/|∇psi|)/(∮ dS/|∇psi|), where R is the pointwise major radius, dS is the surface-area element, and psi is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface. The average is weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient and normalized by the integral of that weight. Its unit is m.
record.documentation: This quantity is the geometric equilibrium coefficient gm8 = <R>_psi, provided as a profile on the poloidal-flux grid. It describes a complete closed magnetic flux surface, rather than the major radius at a selected point such as the inboard midplane, and is not a volume average. It averages R itself, unlike the related coefficients that average 1/R or 1/R²; in particular, 1/<R>_psi generally differs from <1/R>_psi. It applies wherever the stated flux-surface average is well defined and finite.
record.name: flux_surface_averaged_major_radius

record.description: Full vertical extent of the rectangular cross-section of one discrete plasma current-carrying filament element, measured parallel to the Z axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It is h = Z_upper - Z_lower, where Z_upper and Z_lower are the upper and lower cross-section boundaries, and is expressed in m.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the rectangular cross-sectional geometry of an individual filament element representing the axisymmetric plasma current distribution. It is the full vertical dimension, not a half-height or the vertical coordinate of the rectangle's centre. It differs from plasma_filament_width, which measures the full horizontal extent along the major-radius direction, and from thickness_of_plasma_filament, which measures the in-plane extent normal to the filament's central segment. It is a geometric length, not filament current, current density, or cross-sectional area.
record.name: height_of_plasma_filament

record.documentation: The supplied neighbour ethylene_equivalent_electron_source_rate already describes the same instantaneous ethylene injection rate, including the factor of 16 equivalent electrons per molecule. Under the naming rule, that counting convention belongs in the definition, yielding ethylene_source_rate; no source-supported distinction separates the two records.

record.description: Signed rotation of a probing laser beam's linear-polarization orientation induced by crossing magnetized plasma, accumulated from plasma entry to exit along one beam path and expressed in rad. Positive rotation follows the right-hand rule about the beam-propagation direction relative to the incident polarization orientation. The value is obtained either by polarimetric measurement or by calculation from a reconstructed equilibrium along the same path. In the cold, weakly dispersive magnetoionic limit, the electron contribution is α = [e^3 λ^2/(8π^2 ε0 m_e^2 c^3)] ∫ n_e B_parallel dℓ, where λ is the vacuum probing wavelength, e is the elementary-charge magnitude, ε0 is the vacuum permittivity, m_e is the electron mass, c is the speed of light, and B_parallel is signed along beam propagation. The integral covers only the beam segment inside the plasma; rotation from external optics or calibration elements is excluded.
record.documentation: Faraday angle measures plasma-induced rotation of the polarization orientation, not polarization ellipticity, which describes the polarization ellipse's shape, nor the emission polarization orientation measured by the motional Stark effect. It is an accumulated angle along a single probing-beam path, rather than a local rotation rate, a flux-surface average, or an average over channels. Polarimeter channels report this angle, and equilibrium reconstruction uses measured values as constraints and calculates corresponding values from the reconstructed state. Measured and reconstructed values represent the same physical quantity; their difference is a fit residual, not another definition of Faraday angle.
record.name: faraday_angle

record.documentation: The existing weight_of_interferometer_beam record already describes the same per-beam factor weighting a line-integrated electron-density residual in a weighted objective. The case file records no distinguishing quantity or relation. Equilibrium reconstruction specifies its use, not a separate quantity, so retaining equilibrium would not resolve the semantic collision.

record.description: Dimensionless squareness coefficient for the lower, inboard (high-field-side) quadrant of a nested magnetic flux surface, defined according to T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009. It measures signed corner departure from a reference ellipse with the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation: zero denotes no additional lower-inner corner shaping, positive values denote boxier corners, and negative values denote more indented or diamond-like corners. It is a quadrant-specific coefficient, not an average of upper and lower inner squareness, and is supplied as a profile in poloidal flux. Unit: 1.
record.documentation: This scalar characterizes the lower high-field-side corner of each magnetic flux surface on the equilibrium's one-dimensional poloidal-flux grid. The reference ellipse is described in a right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame by R = R0 + a cos θ and Z = Z0 + κa sin θ, where (R0, Z0) is its center, a its horizontal half-width, and κ its elongation. The Luce (2013) convention specifies the shape coefficient; the source does not state a numerical extraction procedure. Unlike upper-inner squareness it describes the lower corner, and unlike lower-outer squareness it describes the inboard rather than outboard corner. It is resolved by flux surface rather than restricted to the plasma boundary, and it is not an upper–lower average of inner squareness.
record.name: lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface

record.description: The toroidal electromotive force at the plasma boundary, defined as the last closed magnetic flux surface bounding the confined plasma. It is obtained from the electric-field circulation V_loop = ∮_C E·dl around a closed toroidal loop C at that boundary and is expressed in V. It includes inductive contributions from both external sources and plasma currents. Positive voltage drives positive ohmic current anticlockwise when viewed from above, corresponding to circulation along increasing toroidal angle φ in a right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the inductive voltage driving resistive plasma current at the last closed flux surface. Unlike average_external_loop_voltage, which represents only the contribution from changing externally applied average poloidal magnetic flux, it includes both external-source and plasma-current contributions. It is an electromotive force around a closed loop, not an electrostatic potential difference between two points, the resulting current_due_to_ohmic_current_drive, or the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the plasma boundary.
record.name: loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary

record.description: Local scalar equal to the reciprocal of the squared Euclidean magnitude of the total equilibrium magnetic-field vector: B^-2 = 1/|B|^2 = 1/(B·B), in T^-2. All field components are included; no component selection, particle-population restriction, flux-surface averaging or volume aggregation is applied.
record.documentation: This magnetic-geometry factor is positive wherever the total magnetic-field magnitude is nonzero and increases as the field weakens; it is undefined at zero field. It differs from the square of magnetic-field magnitude by the reciprocal operation and from a selected component’s reciprocal square by using the full vector magnitude. The [flux-surface-averaged inverse square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude) is obtained by averaging this local factor over a flux surface, rather than by taking the reciprocal of an averaged squared field.
record.name: inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude

record.description: Dimensionless geometric minor-radius label of a magnetic flux surface, obtained as (R_max - R_min)/(2 L_ref), where R_max and R_min are the maximum and minimum major-radius coordinates on the surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, and L_ref is a specified positive reference length. The coordinates and reference length are expressed in m, giving unit 1. This label measures normalized geometric half-width, not normalized toroidal or poloidal magnetic flux.
record.documentation: The quantity labels the flux surface of interest by half its major-radius extent divided by the reference length L_ref. Its value depends on the chosen reference length and is not necessarily one at the plasma boundary. Unlike normalized toroidal and poloidal flux coordinates, it is calculated from surface geometry rather than enclosed magnetic flux; unlike elongation, it describes normalized radial size rather than the ratio of vertical to radial extent.
record.name: normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface

record.description: Minor radius of the plasma boundary is the nonnegative half-width of its full major-radius extent in a poloidal cross-section, calculated as a = (R_max - R_min)/2, in m. R_max and R_min are the maximum and minimum major-radius coordinates over the entire boundary contour in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. The plasma boundary denotes the last closed magnetic flux surface, where psi = psi_LCFS, with psi the poloidal magnetic flux.
record.documentation: This quantity characterizes the horizontal size of the plasma cross-section without assuming a circular contour. It is a single contour-wide geometric size parameter, distinct from the radial outline, which supplies a major-radius coordinate at each boundary point, and from the major-radius coordinate of the geometric axis. It is neither a flux-surface average nor the distance from the magnetic axis to an individual boundary point. The summary source explicitly uses the last closed flux surface; the equilibrium source applies the same half-span calculation to its supplied fixed-boundary contour, typically chosen at normalized poloidal flux of 99.x% of the separatrix value.
record.name: minor_radius_of_plasma_boundary

record.description: Radial flux-surface location of the closed surface selected as the plasma boundary for a fixed-boundary equilibrium, expressed as the linear normalized poloidal flux coordinate. It is obtained as (psi_boundary - psi_axis)/(psi_sep - psi_axis), where psi_boundary is the poloidal magnetic flux on the selected surface, psi_axis is its value at the magnetic axis, and psi_sep is its value at the reference separatrix. The coordinate is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the separatrix; fixed-boundary calculations typically select a value slightly below one. The quantity is dimensionless, with unit 1.
record.documentation: This scalar specifies which closed flux surface is used as the boundary by a fixed-boundary equilibrium calculation. The selected computational boundary may lie just inside the reference last closed flux surface rather than coincide with it. Its label is the linear normalized poloidal flux itself, not its square root or a toroidal-flux-based coordinate. Unlike poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary, which gives the dimensional flux in Wb, this quantity gives a dimensionless flux-surface location; unlike radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary, it does not describe the boundary's geometric contour. It uses the same coordinate convention as normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal but locates the selected plasma boundary rather than the pedestal.
record.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary

record.documentation: No source text is bound to this target. The incumbent supplies a general particle-energy concept, but does not establish a turbulence-specific quantity or justify a physics-group assignment. The family distinguishes a gyrokinetic distribution coordinate from a suprathermal population’s total kinetic energy; neither specialization can be selected without additional source evidence.
record.name: particle_energy

record.description: Perimeter of the complete closed contour formed by one magnetic flux surface in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle, obtained as L = ∮√(dR² + dZ²) in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle and Z is vertical height; expressed in m, with no averaging or summation over surfaces.
record.documentation: This non-negative geometric length measures one complete poloidal circuit of a selected magnetic flux surface, a surface of constant magnetic-flux label. It is not the distance along a magnetic field line, a toroidal circumference, a local arc segment, or a radial or vertical span. Unlike [poloidal-plane cross-sectional area of a flux surface](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface), it measures the contour rather than its enclosed region. Unlike [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), it retains the absolute geometric scale rather than describing a scale-independent shape ratio. The selected surface need not be the last closed flux surface.
record.name: poloidal_length_of_flux_surface

record.description: Length of the minor, beta-inclined side of a plasma-filament element's poloidal parallelogram cross-section, obtained as the Euclidean distance between the side's endpoints and expressed in m. The angle beta is measured relative to the vertical height axis Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. The quantity describes one element, without summation or averaging, and excludes the complementary major, alpha-inclined side.
record.documentation: This scalar specifies the minor oblique side of a single plasma current-carrying filament element. For endpoint position vectors x_beta,1 and x_beta,2, its value is ell_beta = ||x_beta,2 - x_beta,1||, where the norm is the Euclidean norm. It is a straight cross-sectional side length, not a magnetic-field-line length, a filament trajectory length, or a cross-sectional area. The major-side length selects the complementary side inclined relative to the major-radius axis. The neighbouring second_inclination_length_of_plasma_filament describes the same beta-inclined side; the supplied descriptions establish no physical distinction between those two labels.
record.name: minor_length_of_plasma_filament

record.description: Plasma current (Ip) is the net signed conventional electric current flowing toroidally through the plasma column, expressed in A. It is the integral of the toroidal plasma current density over a complete poloidal cross-section, with opposing contributions combined algebraically. Positive current is anti-clockwise when viewed from above. Values may be obtained from magnetic measurements or calculated from a reconstructed equilibrium; the fibre-optic current sensor reports the total toroidal current through the area outlined by its fibre path, measured using the Faraday magneto-optic effect. Unlike population-resolved or flux-surface-enclosed currents, the global plasma quantity includes all plasma charge carriers over the full cross-section.
record.documentation: This is the global toroidal current, not a local current density, a field-parallel current, a runaway-electron contribution, or the current assigned to a single plasma filament. A cumulative toroidal plasma current evaluated at the full plasma boundary recovers the global value. Measured and equilibrium-reconstructed values represent the same physical quantity obtained by different methods; magnetic estimates may provide several calculation methods, with the generally recommended method first. For fibre-optic measurements, the enclosing fibre path specifies the integration area, so the reported enclosed current must be interpreted with that measurement boundary in mind. Currents assigned to external coils or passive structures are distinct quantities.
record.name: plasma_current

record.description: Dimensionless plasma-pressure beta relative to a current-based poloidal magnetic-pressure scale, defined as βp = 4∫V p dV/(R₀ μ₀ Ip²), with unit 1. Here p is the plasma pressure supplied by the source, V is the evaluation volume, R₀ is the reference major radius, μ₀ is vacuum permeability, and Ip is the plasma current used in the normalization. It compares volume-averaged pressure with a poloidal rather than toroidal magnetic-pressure scale.
record.documentation: The global value integrates pressure over the plasma volume; the radial profile evaluates the pressure content inside the corresponding flux surface. Where pressure is obtained from equilibrium reconstruction, the same normalization applies to that reconstructed pressure. In the canonical relation βp = 2μ₀⟨p⟩V/Bp,ref², the volume average is ⟨p⟩V = (1/V)∫V p dV and the effective reference field satisfies Bp,ref² = μ₀²Ip²R₀/(2V). This is a current-based field scale, not a pointwise poloidal field or an average of local pressure-to-field ratios. Unlike toroidal beta, it uses the poloidal magnetic-pressure scale; unlike pedestal electron beta, it is not restricted to local electron thermal pressure. The normalization requires nonzero plasma current and positive evaluation volume.
record.name: poloidal_beta

record.description: Area enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface (LCFS), which defines the plasma boundary, in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It is the integral A = ∫∫_S dR dZ over the complete planar region S enclosed by the LCFS contour, expressed in m^2, rather than the area of the full toroidal magnetic surface.
record.documentation: This global equilibrium scalar measures the plasma cross-sectional size enclosed by the complete plasma-boundary contour. In the defining area integral, R is major radius, phi is toroidal angle, Z is vertical height, and S is the planar interior of the LCFS contour at fixed phi. It is the plasma-boundary specialization of poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface, which applies to an arbitrary closed magnetic flux surface. It is not a contour length, a local surface element, a flux-surface average, or the surface area obtained by sweeping the contour toroidally.
record.name: poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_boundary

record.description: Signed magnetic flux through a surface bounded by the contour formed by intersecting the magnetic surface through the evaluation point with a plane of constant vertical coordinate Z. For a flat integration surface, the normal points upward, toward increasing Z. In axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates, the full flux is ψ(R,Z) = 2π ∫₀ᴿ B_Z(R′,Z) R′ dR′, in Wb, where B_Z is the vertical magnetic-field component. This is the full surface integral, not flux divided by 2π, a normalized coordinate, or a spatial average.
record.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux, commonly denoted ψ or Φ_p, labels magnetic surfaces in axisymmetric equilibrium and can be represented on spatial grids or used as a radial profile coordinate. In axisymmetry, its integration surface is a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle through the evaluation point; upward magnetic-field threading contributes positively. Unlike toroidal magnetic flux, it does not integrate the toroidal field through a poloidal cross-section. It includes plasma-generated and external contributions, rather than selecting only external flux. This record describes the general flux function, not its evaluation at a designated magnetic axis, plasma boundary, measurement position, or individual flux loop.
record.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux

record.description: Poloidal magnetic flux evaluated at the magnetic axis of an axisymmetric equilibrium, expressed in Wb. In the right-handed cylindrical frame (R, φ, Z), it is Φ_p,a = Φ_p(R_a, Z_a) = 2π∫₀^{R_a} B_Z(R′, Z_a) R′ dR′, the signed flux through the horizontal disk bounded by the toroidal circle at the magnetic-axis coordinates (R_a, Z_a). The sign is positive for net flux directed toward increasing Z. This unnormalized equilibrium value includes both external-source and plasma-current contributions and need not be zero. Its locus is the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes at the O-point inside nested closed flux surfaces, rather than the plasma boundary or another evaluation position.
record.documentation: The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. This quantity is the value of the poloidal magnetic-flux function there, not a toroidal flux, a magnetic-field component, or a weighted external-only flux. Together with the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary, Φ_p,b, it supplies the physical reference values for the dimensionless poloidal-flux fraction (Φ_p − Φ_p,a)/(Φ_p,b − Φ_p,a), provided the denominator is nonzero. That fraction is zero at the axis and one at the boundary; the reference values remain applicable when a radial grid does not reach either endpoint. The quantity recorded here is the dimensional axis flux itself, not the normalized fraction.
record.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis

record.description: Major-radius coordinate R of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard, high-field-side midplane intersection, expressed in m. It is obtained by evaluating the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis at that intersection in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. Under the inboard-midplane convention, this is the surface's minimum major radius, on the inboard side of the magnetic axis.
record.documentation: This quantity gives one inboard-midplane major-radius value for each magnetic flux surface in the equilibrium profile indexed by poloidal flux. It specializes radial_coordinate by fixing the evaluation locus to the high-field-side midplane, rather than the outboard, low-field-side midplane represented by radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane. It locates a point on a flux surface, not the magnetic axis itself, and is neither a minor-radius distance from that axis nor a flux-surface average.
record.name: radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane

record.description: Total non-negative power deposited on a single divertor target by recombination at the plasma-material interface, obtained by summing the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination contributions for that target. It is inferred from edge-plasma simulations or particle-flux measurements combined with surface energy-release models and is expressed in W.
record.documentation: This scalar includes both the plasma-ion neutralization contribution and the neutral-particle surface-recombination contribution, including molecular formation. It therefore differs from plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination and neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination, which describe the individual channels. Its scope is one divertor target, rather than all targets in the divertor assembly as in power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination, or plasma-facing materials without a specified location as in power_due_to_recombination. It represents deposited power, not power density or the total target heat load from all processes.
record.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination

record.description: Major-radius coordinate of the plasma-current centroid in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, obtained as R_c = ∫_Dp R j_φ dS / I_p, where Dp is the plasma current-carrying poloidal cross-section, j_φ is the toroidal plasma-current density, dS is a poloidal area element, and I_p = ∫_Dp j_φ dS is the total toroidal plasma current. Expressed in m.
record.documentation: This quantity gives the radial position of the centroid of the full toroidal plasma-current distribution, using its major-radius first moment normalized by the total plasma current. The weighting is by toroidal current density, not geometric area, particle density, pressure, or magnetic-field strength, so the current center is distinct from the plasma's geometric center and need not coincide with the magnetic axis. It is a locus-specific radial_coordinate; vertical_coordinate_of_current_center provides the corresponding vertical position rather than the major-radius position.
record.name: radial_coordinate_of_current_center

record.description: Real part of the radial component of the perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region outside the plasma, obtained from linear MHD stability analysis for a specified toroidal mode number. It is Re(Ã_vac · e_R), where e_R points toward increasing major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, and the real part is taken relative to the complex eigenfunction's phase reference. The unit is T.m.
record.documentation: This quantity describes one toroidal mode of the vacuum magnetic vector-potential perturbation in linear magnetohydrodynamic stability analysis, not gyrokinetics. It retains only the real radial component, rather than the imaginary component or the full complex radial quantity, and is not a sum over modes. Positive values indicate a real projection toward increasing major radius. It differs from the poloidal plasma vector-potential component in both direction and region, and from the radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field because it is a vector potential rather than a magnetic field. The source does not specify an eigenfunction normalization or an absolute phase reference.
record.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part

record.documentation: The supplied definition identifies the same quantity as the existing neighbour poloidal_plane_outer_cross_sectional_radius_of_plasma_filament: the distance from the center of the filament’s annular poloidal cross-section to its outer circular conducting boundary. No physical distinction between these quantities is supplied. The additional cross-sectional and poloidal-plane wording does not distinguish a different radius, so a separate record would duplicate that neighbour.
record.name: outer_radius_of_plasma_filament

record.description: Local scalar equilibrium metric coefficient obtained as G = |∇ρ_tor|^2/R^2, where ρ_tor is the length-valued toroidal-flux coordinate at its prescribed scale, ∇ is the spatial gradient, and the magnitude is the Euclidean norm. R is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. No boundary normalization, substitution of an arbitrary flux label, or spatial averaging is applied. The unit is m^-2.
record.documentation: This coefficient describes local flux-surface spacing with inverse-square major-radius weighting. Its defining relation is G = |∇ρ_tor|^2/R^2; the gradient of the length-valued coordinate is dimensionless, giving G units of m^-2. Unlike square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude, it includes division by squared major radius; unlike the magnetic-field-denominator family member, its denominator is R squared rather than magnetic-field magnitude squared. The gradient factor also distinguishes it from inverse squared major radius alone. The neighbour flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius averages this complete local ratio over a closed magnetic flux surface, rather than dividing separately averaged numerator and denominator.
record.name: ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius

record.description: Signed major-radius separation, in m, between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix there: ΔR = R_mapped − R_sep,mid. The mapping preserves the measurement position's magnetic flux label. Major radius R is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame; the outboard midplane is the low-field-side point of maximum R on the relevant flux surface. The separation is positive outside the separatrix on the scrape-off-layer side, zero on the separatrix, and negative on the confined-plasma side.
record.documentation: This scalar locates a measurement relative to the separatrix using a common outboard-midplane reference, independently of the measurement's original position. It is obtained by subtracting the major radius of the outboard-midplane separatrix intersection from that of the flux-surface-mapped measurement position. It is a dimensional difference of major radii, not a normalized magnetic flux coordinate, a radial coordinate assigned to a flux surface, an unmapped local separation, or the shortest distance normal to the separatrix. The same quantity applies to embedded and reciprocating Langmuir probes and Thomson-scattering channels.
record.name: radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane

record.description: Full non-negative clear-aperture extent of an optical element along X2, its second object-local tangential axis, measured in m. For rectangular aperture geometry (geometry_type = 3), it is the difference between opposing aperture-edge coordinates, w = X2_max - X2_min, and denotes the full width rather than the half-width.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the usable rectangular opening of an optical element, not the element's external dimensions or opaque mounting structures. It applies only when geometry_type = 3. In the object-local aperture plane (X1, X2), the width spans the opposing edges along X2; the first local tangential width instead spans X1. Unlike a second local tangential coordinate, which specifies a signed position relative to the local origin, this width is a non-negative edge-to-edge extent. The locus is the optical element's aperture, rather than a separately specified aperture or polarizer.
record.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_optical_element

record.description: Complex scalar E-minus component of the coherent wave electric field in the plane perpendicular to the static magnetic field, designated right-hand circularly polarized by the source. It is obtained from the full-wave-code solution for each wave frequency and time slice, with one scalar value per element of a generic-grid subset, and is expressed in V.m^-1.
record.documentation: This quantity retains the amplitude and phase of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus wave electric-field component, rather than representing a vector contribution, its amplitude alone, or its imaginary quadrature. The source identifies this component as driving ion cyclotron resonance heating and contributing to wave–particle coupling. Handedness is referenced to the static magnetic field; no explicit circular-basis normalization or temporal phasor convention is specified. It is distinct from the complementary left-hand E-plus component, the parallel wave electric field, and non-wave contributions to the total electric field. Values are supplied locally on generic-grid subsets, rather than being restricted to a beam or ray path or to a single toroidal-mode contribution.
record.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field

record.description: Spectral photon radiance is the calibrated directional photon arrival rate from plasma emission per projected collecting area, viewing solid angle, and wavelength interval. It is defined by dN_gamma = L_gamma(lambda) dt dA_perp dOmega dlambda, where A_perp is the collecting area projected perpendicular to the ray direction. It is expressed per unit wavelength, not per frequency or photon-energy interval, in m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1.
record.documentation: This quantity describes the absolute photon-number brightness of plasma radiation along a specified viewing direction, resolved by wavelength. It includes the line and continuum contributions present at that wavelength without restriction to an emitting species or radiation mechanism; spectral bremsstrahlung photon radiance instead selects only the free-free contribution. Unlike photon radiance at a spectral line, it is a wavelength-resolved density rather than a background-subtracted integral over an identified line. It is neither a local volumetric photon-production rate, an energy radiance, nor an uncalibrated detector count rate.
record.name: spectral_photon_radiance
