record.description: Full transverse side length of the rectangular cross-section representing a discrete plasma current-carrying filament element, specified in the thick-line geometry perpendicular to its central segment within the cross-sectional plane. It is a full thickness, not a half-width, and is measured in m. Unlike radial width or vertical height, its direction is defined relative to the central segment rather than a fixed machine axis.
record.documentation: The thick-line representation approximates a plasma filament element's cross-section by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a perpendicular thickness. The thickness is the full separation between the rectangle's sides parallel to that segment; the complementary side length runs along the segment. These two full side lengths multiply to give the cross-sectional area. The local transverse direction lies in the poloidal plane and need not coincide with either the radial direction used for plasma filament width or the vertical direction used for plasma filament height. This quantity describes the geometry of a discrete element used to represent the axisymmetric plasma current distribution.
record.name: thickness_of_plasma_filament

record.description: Dimensionless signed safety factor q at the magnetic axis, obtained as q_axis = lim(rho→0) q(rho), where rho labels nested closed magnetic flux surfaces and vanishes at the axis. On neighboring surfaces, q is the number of toroidal field-line turns per complete poloidal circuit: q = (1/(2π)) ∮ (B·∇φ)/(B·∇θ) dθ, with B the magnetic field, φ the toroidal angle and θ the poloidal angle. The integral covers one poloidal circuit in axisymmetry or straight-field-line flux coordinates. The toroidal angle is measured in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above; q is positive when φ advances as θ increases. The axis value is a limit, not a direct evaluation of the poloidal-angle integral at the axis. Unit: 1.
record.documentation: The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged; in an axisymmetric equilibrium it passes through the O-point where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes. This quantity specifies the safety factor at that locus, rather than on an unspecified flux surface, at the pedestal, at an internal transport barrier or at the plasma boundary. It is neither a spatial average nor the minimum safety factor over the equilibrium domain, which need not occur at the axis. It is also distinct from magnetic shear at the axis, which describes variation of the safety factor rather than its value.
record.name: safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis

record.description: Azimuthal coordinate of a point on a control surface about the machine symmetry axis, expressed in rad in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is defined by φ = atan2(y, x) modulo 2π, with zero set by the facility-defined reference direction and positive angles increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above along the +Z axis toward the origin. The source supplies these coordinates as the toroidal angle array on which the Fourier decomposition of the normal magnetic field is carried out.
record.documentation: This quantity locates control-surface points in the toroidal direction; it is not the toroidal angle of a launching position, outlet, diagnostic measurement position, or antenna strap. It is an angular coordinate rather than the control surface's major-radius or vertical coordinate, and it is not a magnetic-field component or an angular offset from a reference position. The source stores a one-dimensional array of these angles for the control-surface Fourier decomposition. Angles differing by an integer multiple of 2π identify the same toroidal direction.
record.name: toroidal_angle_of_control_surface

record.description: Signed toroidal orientation angle of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil’s sensitive-axis normal, expressed in rad. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame it is obtained as atan2(n_φ, n_R), where n_R and n_φ are the radial and toroidal components of that normal. It is measured from +R toward the normal’s horizontal projection, positive toward increasing φ; zero corresponds to an outward-directed projection in the poloidal plane.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the orientation of an individual poloidal magnetic-field probe coil, not its toroidal position around the machine or the magnetic field it measures. It specifies the toroidal orientation of the sensitive axis rather than its poloidal tilt, and differs from the corresponding toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe by the type of sensor described. The orientation is part of the probe geometry used to relate its measured field component to the local magnetic-field vector; it is not averaged over probes, turns, or field samples.
record.name: toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe

record.description: Signed toroidal component of the total equilibrium magnetic field evaluated locally at the magnetic axis, obtained from the equilibrium reconstruction as B_phi,axis = B_axis · e_phi, in T. The total field includes external-coil and plasma-current contributions. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, e_phi points toward increasing phi, with phi = atan2(y, x), so positive values indicate counterclockwise field when viewed from above.
record.documentation: This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the equilibrium magnetic field at the magnetic axis, the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. In an axisymmetric poloidal cross-section, the axis is the O-point where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes. It is distinct from the magnetic-field magnitude, the vacuum field that omits plasma-current contributions, and the toroidal reference field evaluated at a reference point. Unlike the toroidal magnetic field at a specified flux-surface point, its evaluation locus is specifically the magnetic axis; no flux-surface averaging is applied.
record.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis

record.description: Signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at the designated reference point whose major radius is the reference major radius. It is obtained as B_phi,ref = B_eq(x_ref) · e_phi(x_ref), where e_phi points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. Positive values indicate that direction. The quantity is supplied as a dimensional normalization reference for local gyrokinetic calculations and is expressed in T.
record.documentation: This scalar is the reference-location specialization of toroidal magnetic field and the toroidal projection of the reference magnetic-field vector, rather than its magnitude. The full reference point specifies the evaluation location; its major radius alone does not generally determine the field. For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the value is independent of the reference toroidal angle. The reference location need not be the magnetic axis or a specified flux-surface location. Unlike toroidal vacuum magnetic field, this quantity is not restricted to the external-current contribution. Its role in normalization does not make it dimensionless or imply an average.
record.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field

record.description: Signed toroidal component of the total conventional electric current density, obtained as j_phi = e_phi · j_tot = sum_k(e_phi · j_k), where the included current contributions are summed algebraically rather than by magnitude. The unit vector e_phi points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, so positive values indicate conventional charge transport in that direction. It is provided as one scalar value per element of the specified generalized-grid subset, in A.m^-2.
record.documentation: This quantity fixes the common signed projection of total current density to the toroidal direction, rather than the radial, poloidal, or field-aligned direction. It represents the total of the included current contributions, not a contribution selected by particle species, orbit class, or current-generation mechanism. The bound sources provide this component on generalized-grid subsets for edge-plasma, plasma-profile, and wall-physics quantities; the name therefore imposes no plasma-only or wall-only locus. It is a grid-resolved component, not the current-density magnitude, a flux-surface average, or a spatially integrated current.
record.name: toroidal_total_current_density

record.documentation: The bound sources describe distinct counting bases. The three intensity_spectrum sources specify photoelectrons detected per unit time at each wavelength pixel, with electronic gain compensation and relative channel calibration applied but without absolute calibration. The filter-spectrometer photon_count source instead specifies detected photons, with unit s^-1, and does not establish a per-wavelength-pixel quantity or the same corrections. Photon and photoelectron detection rates cannot be identified without a conversion relation that the sources do not supply. These sources must be separated before a single standard-name record can be defined.
record.name: spectral_rate_of_spectrometer_channel

record.description: Total non-inductive auxiliary power coupled to the whole plasma, obtained by summing the coupled-power contributions from neutral-beam injection, electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid systems, excluding Ohmic power. It is expressed in W.
record.documentation: This quantity aggregates the external auxiliary power input over all included heating systems, rather than resolving it by source, plasma species, or spatial region. It may contribute to both plasma heating and non-inductive current drive and is therefore not restricted to energy deposited as particle internal energy. Unlike overall plasma heating power, it excludes Ohmic heating and internally generated fusion heating; unlike source-specific powers, it combines all included auxiliary systems. It measures power coupled to the plasma, not generator output or power merely launched toward the plasma.
record.name: external_heating_power

record.description: Signed toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the selected plasma boundary, obtained as Phi_tor,b = integral over Omega_b of B_phi dA_RZ, where Omega_b is that cross-section and B_phi is the total toroidal magnetic-field component. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, positive flux corresponds to field in the direction of increasing phi, counter-clockwise when viewed from above +Z. The flux includes externally imposed and plasma-poloidal-current contributions, without normalization or division by 2*pi. Its unit is Wb.
record.documentation: This scalar is the boundary value of toroidal magnetic flux, rather than its value on an arbitrary interior flux surface. The source records it at equilibrium/time_slice/boundary/phi for the selected boundary used by fixed-boundary codes, typically chosen at normalized poloidal flux of 99.x% of the separatrix value; the selected computational boundary therefore need not coincide exactly with the last closed magnetic flux surface. Unlike toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current, it is not restricted to the plasma-current contribution. Unlike poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary, it integrates the toroidal field through a poloidal cross-section, not the poloidal field through a horizontal disk.
record.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary

record.description: Vertical (Z) coordinate of the position at which a measurement used to constrain equilibrium reconstruction is given, expressed in m. It is the signed height relative to the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with Z = x·ẑ, where x is the position vector from the coordinate origin and ẑ points upward parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. The locus is specifically a constraint position rather than a general measurement position.
record.documentation: This scalar locates an individual equilibrium-reconstruction constraint vertically, including constraints on parallel current density, toroidal current density, or total plasma pressure. Positive Z denotes a position above the zero-height plane. It describes the position associated with the constraint, not the constrained observable, its reconstructed value, or a magnetic-flux surface label. Any flux-surface averaging used to define a current-density constraint applies to that observable, not to this height coordinate.
record.name: vertical_coordinate_of_constraint_position

record.description: Dimensionless shape parameter of the plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section, obtained as the arithmetic mean of its upper and lower triangularities: δ = [(R_geo − R_u)/a + (R_geo − R_l)/a]/2. Here R_geo is the major radius of the geometric axis, R_u and R_l are the major radii of the upper and lower vertical extrema, and a is the boundary minor radius, using right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) coordinates. Inward offsets are positive and outward offsets are negative. The unit is 1.
record.documentation: Plasma-boundary triangularity describes the normalized inward radial displacement of the boundary’s vertical extrema, combining both extrema into one shape parameter. The plasma boundary denotes the last closed magnetic flux surface bounding the confined plasma. Unlike upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary and lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary, which each use only one vertical extremum, this quantity is their arithmetic mean and can therefore conceal differences between the upper and lower shapes. It differs from triangularity_of_flux_surface by describing the plasma boundary rather than an individual nested flux surface, and from elongation or squareness by measuring extremal radial displacement rather than vertical-to-radial extent or corner shape.
record.name: triangularity_of_plasma_boundary

record.description: Signed vertical coordinate of the plasma-current centroid in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured in m. It is obtained as Z_c = integral_A(Z j_φ dA) / I_p, where A is the poloidal cross-section carrying plasma current, j_φ is toroidal current density, and I_p = integral_A(j_φ dA) is total plasma current. Positive values place the centroid in the +Z direction from the coordinate origin, parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.
record.documentation: This scalar is the toroidal-current-density-weighted centroid height, not the height of the magnetic axis or a geometric center. The poloidal cross-sectional first moment of toroidal current is normalized by total plasma current. It describes the vertical rather than radial coordinate of the current center and is a position rather than the vertical velocity of that center.
record.name: vertical_coordinate_of_current_center

record.description: Vertical coordinate Z, in m, of the specified geometry point of a plasma filament: the reference point from which alpha and beta are defined for an oblique parallelogram cross-section, or the second endpoint of the central segment for a thick-line rectangular cross-section. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, Z = x · ẑ, where x is the point's position relative to the coordinate origin and ẑ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis; Z is positive on the positive-Z side of the zero-height plane.
record.documentation: This quantity locates a geometry point of one discrete current-carrying plasma filament used to represent the axisymmetric plasma current distribution. For an oblique cross-section it gives the height of the reference point anchoring the alpha and beta angles; for a thick-line cross-section it gives the height of the second endpoint of the rectangle's central segment. It is a vertical point coordinate, rather than the radial coordinate, a cross-sectional length or thickness, or the vertical outline coordinates describing the filament contour. It is not an average over filaments or a coordinate of the plasma boundary.
record.name: vertical_coordinate_of_plasma_filament

record.description: Number density of tungsten ions, obtained by summing the number densities of all positive tungsten charge states: n_W = sum from Z = 1 to 74 of n_W^(Z+). Each ion is counted once, without charge weighting, and neutral tungsten is excluded. The quantity may be evaluated locally or spatially averaged over a specified domain; no particular locus or averaging operation is prescribed. Its unit is m^-3.
record.documentation: Tungsten density describes the concentration of positively charged tungsten ions rather than neutral tungsten, a single charge-state population, or a tungsten-to-electron density ratio. Unlike the volume-averaged, line-averaged and locus-specific tungsten-density quantities, this general quantity does not prescribe an averaging domain or evaluation location. Any spatial average must specify its domain and averaging convention while retaining the sum over positive charge states.
record.name: tungsten_density

record.description: Volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface, obtained as V = ∫_Ω d³x over its entire interior Ω and expressed in m^3. A flux surface consists of points sharing the same magnetic-flux label; in the stated poloidal-flux convention, ψ(R, Z) = const, where ψ is poloidal magnetic flux. This is the cumulative enclosed volume, not the shell volume between adjacent surfaces or a derivative with respect to a flux coordinate.
record.documentation: The selected flux surface is not restricted to the pedestal top or plasma boundary, and it is distinct from the first-wall surface. Differences between enclosed volumes give the volume of the intervening shell. For successively enclosing nested surfaces, V increases from zero at the magnetic axis. At the plasma boundary it equals the total confined-plasma volume, while at the pedestal-top surface it equals the volume enclosed by that surface. Derivatives of V with respect to poloidal or toroidal flux coordinates describe changes in enclosed volume rather than the volume itself.
record.name: volume_of_flux_surface

record.description: Dimensionless scalar factor assigned to the residual between modeled and reference line-integrated electron density for a single interferometer beam, controlling that residual's relative contribution to a weighted objective. For a quadratic objective, the beam contribution is Phi_b = w_b r_b^2, where w_b is this weight and r_b is the beam residual. The weight is assigned per beam; no averaging or normalization across beams is implied. Unit: 1.
record.documentation: This quantity weights one interferometer beam's line-integrated electron-density constraint, rather than an entire interferometer system or another constraint type. It is neither the electron density nor its residual or uncertainty. It is the general parent of equilibrium_weight_of_interferometer_beam, which restricts the same weighting role to an equilibrium objective. No particular procedure for selecting the weight or normalizing the residual is specified.
record.name: weight_of_interferometer_beam

record.documentation: The source describes the outline of a boundary used by fixed-boundary equilibrium codes, typically chosen at psi_norm = 99.x% of the separatrix. The supplied registry and ruled convention instead require plasma_boundary to mean the last closed magnetic flux surface. These loci are not generally identical, so the source quantity cannot be assigned the proposed name without resolving this registry conflict.

The bound sources do not determine one quantity. Most describe vertical position coordinates, but ece/channel/delta_position_suprathermal/z describes a vertical displacement correction, with uncorrected position = position − delta_position_suprathermal. Other sources describe beamlet or diagnostic-component geometry rather than the registered measurement_position locus. The multiple-collector average position is also explicitly averaged, although no averaging rule is supplied. These sources must be separated before a single name and definition can identify the quantity without contradicting its source.

record.description: Vertical coordinate Z of a grid location, expressed in m in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, with the vertical direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. The value gives the height of the grid location, rather than a radial coordinate or an angular coordinate.
record.documentation: These values describe the vertical geometry of computational grids, including the non-axisymmetric magnetic-field map grid, equilibrium and vacuum-mode flux-surface coordinate grids, and equilibrium generic-grid subsets. The flux-surface coordinate grids store height on a square grid of flux and poloidal angle; the generic-grid representation provides one scalar height per grid-subset element. The quantity describes grid locations, not the position of a camera, measurement point, vessel, or other physical component, and does not denote the height of a coordinate-system origin.
record.name: vertical_coordinate_of_grid

record.description: The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an elliptic shatter cone, obtained as e_maj,y = e_hat_maj · y_hat in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame. The full major-axis vector has unit magnitude; this component is positive when it points toward +y and is dimensionless, with unit 1.
record.documentation: This scalar describes the y projection of the major-semiaxis orientation of the elliptic shatter cone associated with a shattered-pellet injector. It is an individual vector component, not an average or integral. Together with the x and z components it specifies the major-axis unit vector, whose squared components sum to one. It differs from the y component of the minor-axis unit vector and from the y component of the cone-direction unit vector by the geometric direction being described; it is neither a major-axis length nor the major half-opening angle.
record.name: y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
